Proposed taxonomy (6 dimensions with example indicators): (1) Temporal depth—explicit step count in plan, % of plans with multi-step decomposition; (2) Goal decomposition & fidelity—#subtasks identified, correctness/coverage vs. gold decomposition; (3) Action sequencing & coherence—ordering validity score, contradiction rate between steps; (4) Contingency & adaptivity—detection of failure conditions, presence and quality of fallback branches; (5) Resource/constraint management—feasibility score given stated constraints, violations of budget/time/resource limits; (6) Safety/transparency signals—presence of unsafe recommendations, explicit rationale or provenance for each step.  

Standard scenario template (fields to complete for every v1 case): Title; Application class (customer‑support or workflow/scheduling); short context & user goal; initial state and explicit constraints; allowed model interactions (one-shot, multi-turn); success criteria and “good‑enough” thresholds (functional and UX); target planning behaviors (taxonomy dims engaged); concrete prompts and example oracle outputs; metrics mapped to taxonomy indicators; enumerated expected failure modes to track; reproducibility notes (model, API, seeds).  

To distinguish application classes and adequacy: require scenario-specific thresholds in the template (e.g., customer‑support: correct resolution within ≤3 exchanges and preserves stated intent; workflow/scheduling: produced schedule meets all hard constraints and ≥X% utilization/efficiency); failures to track include omission of necessary steps, unsafe or infeasible actions, poor contingency plans, and lack of provenance.  

Policy-readiness: mark dimensions likely to attract regulatory attention (contingency/adaptivity, resource/constraint violations, safety/transparency) and ensure each indicator is operationalizable (clear measurement procedure, reproducibility notes) so outputs can be defended to standards bodies.  

How this enables scaling and governance: a consistent taxonomy + template lets the RA produce comparable, instrumented scenarios that seed Phase 2 benchmark selection and metric calibration, provides immediate baseline data for prioritizing which behaviors to scale or mitigate, and yields audit-ready artifacts (indicators, provenance, failure cases) feeding later governance case studies.
